claims.text: The initial material is a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy, exemplified by Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V, with high configurational entropy.
Standard experimental melting data are unavailable for the target alloy.
Ab initio free-energy calculations for the target alloy are computationally prohibitive.
An MTP can be trained on cDFT configurations incorporating geometric relaxation, lattice compression or extension, atomic displacements, and magnetic-moment perturbations.
A single-reference thermodynamic-perturbation scheme can replace full phase-space thermodynamic integration for melting calculations.
An MTP trained with high-temperature liquid-like configurations will predict the Ta-based alloy's melting temperature within 2% of an ab initio benchmark.
Including liquid-like configurations in training prevents a frozen-structure artifact common to standard EAM potentials.
Near-solidus and liquidus simulations with sufficient system size and strain-rate selection will capture liquid-structure fluctuations.
Binary interaction complexity in an N-component alloy scales as (N/2)(N-1).
Magnetic-moment arrangements and local lattice distortions can be represented as degrees of freedom by an MTP.
Representing magnetic moments and local distortions allows the MTP to distinguish stable BCC solids from disordered liquids.
Standard EAM potentials can misrepresent multicomponent liquids as amorphous or crystalline artifacts.
Learning magnetic and structural perturbations enables the MTP to reproduce the subtle energy landscape of the liquid phase.
The learned liquid energy landscape enables efficient and accurate evaluation of solid-liquid free-energy differences while avoiding the purported exponential cost of full thermodynamic integration.
Standard EAM potentials will produce melting-temperature deviations greater than 10% because they model the liquid structure incorrectly.
The proposed melting workflow will identify a strength-ductility trade-off in the liquid-to-solid transition region.
The method is applicable to refractory BCC HEAs containing three to six principal elements when magnetic moments are non-negligible.
The method may fail when strong covalent bonding dominates the liquid and is absent from the cDFT training set.
A magnetic cDFT training strategy demonstrated for Fe-Al may not transfer directly to Ta-based refractory alloys without substantial retraining because their electronic and magnetic behavior differs.
The computational efficiency gain depends on convergence of liquid-phase sampling, which is not guaranteed across all multicomponent compositions.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis presents a Ta-alloy MTP whose training explicitly includes high-temperature liquid configurations, while the uncertainty field characterizes the relevant cDFT training set as one focused on magnetic perturbations in Fe-Al. It is unclear whether a new Ta-specific liquid training set is proposed or whether the Fe-Al set is being transferred.

The quantitative prediction is accuracy within 2%, but the stated falsification threshold is deviation greater than 5%. Results between 2% and 5% would violate the prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
